what_happened: The job was meant to make the decisions page list only open proposals that are above the raising role's limit. The verifier rejected it at the final verdict. One of 6 acceptance criteria was unmet: a test through locate() on a temp git repo must show decided proposals absent from the page, and the recorded check output must show that test failing on the old code and passing on the new. No checks are listed as failed. There were three major findings and no blocker. (1) The changelog guesses why decided proposals appeared on the 3 Nov page. The real records and history contradict the guess, and it proposes an out-of-scope fix, a schedule trigger in pages.yml. (2) The changelog calls ne91 a within-limit proposal "nobody had to decide", but ne91 has an approval record. (3) No recorded run shows the new locate() test failing on the old code, because the base already excludes decided proposals, so the test cannot show they are newly excluded.
cause: This is a retry of the "fix wrong page output" work, and nothing in the system makes the root cause a required, evidenced result. The reading asked for a fail-before, pass-after test, but Athena's checks run once on the final tree. There is no recorded run on the old code. So the producer could neither show a reproduction nor notice that the base already excluded decided proposals, which means the symptom came from somewhere else (a stale published page or a data source). Without a reproduction, the changelog filled the gap with a guessed cause and unchecked examples. No step checks changelog claims against the records or history before the final verdict. The "fails without the fix" criterion also needs evidence the verifier cannot observe, which is the same trap as in the earlier rejections.
prevention: Two changes together. First, for bug-fix jobs, Athena runs the new tests on the base tree on a scratch copy before the producer edits code, and records the result. If a test passes on the base, the job must say the bug is not reproduced and find the real cause (for example a stale published page or the data source) before any filter change. Second, the reading must require a named root cause with evidence from the real records, and the changelog may only state causes and examples that the recorded evidence supports. Then a "fails on old code" criterion has an evidence source the verifier can see, and guesses cannot reach the changelog.
proposed_request: Find out why decided (approved or rejected) proposals appeared on the decisions page published on 3 Nov, using the real records branch and the page's build and publish history. Name the cause with evidence from the records, such as the proposal ids and the commit or run that produced that page. Then fix that cause so the page lists only open proposals above the raising role's limit. First run the test on the unchanged base. If decided proposals are already excluded there, do not add a filter. Fix the real cause instead, for example a stale or unrefreshed publish, and keep any workflow change inside the stated deliverables. Add a test through locate() on a temp git repo with a records branch and decision records written where approve-work and reject-work write them. It must fail on the cause as found, and Athena must record the run on the old code and the run on the new. The changelog may state only the cause and examples shown by those records, and must not describe a proposal as undecided if it has an approval or rejection record. Run: cargo test -p xtask decisions.
